title: Decision: Exact string equality for identity comparison
description: Why this is good: The code compares user IDs using == only; never parses, normalizes, or formats them. UserProfile.ID is explicitly opaque in the design document — it varies by Tailscale deployment (numeric ID, UUID, or Headscale-specific format). By treating IDs as uninterpreted strings, the code avoids a common attack surface: someone could exploit differences in parsing/normalization between this code and Tailscale's WhoIs service (e.g., case folding, Unicode normalization, leading zeros). The check_sender() function explicitly documents this ('Comparison is exact string equality only — never normalize or parse'). This defensive pattern prevents subtle spoofing if the ID format ever changes or if an attacker crafts a specially-formatted claim.
